grounding.establishes: Footnote *1 'When discharging.' attaches to MEASUREMENT FREQUENCY column entries for (*1)-marked parameters, not to numeric effluent limit values.
Intermittent-flow outfall 001 authorizes episodic backwash discharges that remain subject to stated limits and monitoring schedules when discharge occurs.
When no discharge occurs during a sampling month, the permittee marks NO DISCHARGE on the DMR instead of performing discharge-conditioned monitoring for that month.
Narrative permit basis confirms monitoring frequencies (flow daily when discharging, pH weekly when discharging, TRC daily when discharging, TDS/cyanide quarterly) are tied to discharge occurrence.
Structured encoding carries DMR_COMMENT_TEXT='WHEN DISCHARGING.' with OPTIONAL_MONITORING_FLAG=N, refuting optional-monitoring-flag semantics for this comment.

interpretation: The permit-limit comment 'WHEN DISCHARGING.' qualifies monitoring-frequency obligations for (*1)-marked parameters: stated frequencies apply only on days or periods when the outfall is discharging. Numeric effluent limits are not suspended by the comment; they govern authorized discharges when discharge occurs. When no discharge occurs during a sampling month, discharge-conditioned monitoring is not required and the permittee reports no discharge on the DMR instead. The comment is not encoded as optional monitoring (OPTIONAL_MONITORING_FLAG remains N).
remaining_uncertainty: Structured sources do not record whether discharge occurred in any FY2025 monitoring period for NM0028762. No NODI_CODE values appear in dmr_measurements.csv for these rows, so no-discharge reporting cannot be observed structurally. The permit does not define a machine-readable rule for aggregating compliance across partial discharge within a month or quarter (e.g., how many discharge days satisfy weekly monitoring).
